rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding boron (<1 wt%) to refractory high-entropy alloys, while the target paper added 4.2 at.% Cr to HfMoTaTiZr. These are different elements, making it a different specific lever.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature (>1000°C) and high-stress (>500 MPa) conditions, whereas the target paper performed room-temperature compression testing. These are contradictory regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes grain-boundary pinning by boride precipitates to improve high-temperature strength and creep resistance. The target paper's mechanism involves solid-solution hardening and crack-propagation hindrance by a reticulated Laves phase. These are different general classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance with maintained room-temperature ductility. The target paper reports concurrent increases in room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain. The property (room-temperature vs. high-temperature) and direction differ.
